title: Palestine Soup
description: A soup made with veal, calf's foot, and chorissa.
steps: Stew a knuckle of veal, a calf's foot, {{source-2}}, and a large fowl, in four quarts of water
Add a piece of fresh lemon-peel, six Jerusalem artichokes, a bunch of sweet herbs, a little salt and white pepper, a nutmeg, and a blade of mace

title: Patent Yeast
description: Prepared with yeast, hops, and malt.

ingredients.name: half a peck of ground malt
ingredients.sourceText: half a peck of ground malt

steps: Boil {{source-0}} in three gallons of water for three hours
Strain it off, and let it stand ten minutes
Add half a peck of ground malt, stir it well up, and cover it over
Return the hops, and put the same quantity of water to them again, boiling them the same time as before
Strain it off to the first mash
Stir it up and let it remain four hours
Strain it off, and set it to work at 90° with three pints of patent yeast
Let it stand about twenty hours
Take the scum off the top, and strain it through a hair sieve
It will then be fit for use. One pint is sufficient to make a bushel of bread.

title: Potato Beer
description: Prepared with potatoes, malt, and hops.

ingredients.name: Eighty quarts of water per scheffel of potatoes
ingredients.sourceText: Eighty quarts of water per scheffel of potatoes

steps: Wash the potatoes well
Rub down the potatoes by a grating cylinder into a hopper
Crush and grind them into pulp
Put eighty quarts of water with each scheffel of potatoes into a copper and make to boil
Work twelve scheffels of crushed malt in the mash-tub with ninety gallons of cold water to a thick pap
Suddenly introduce six barrels of cold water with constant stirring and let stand an hour at rest
When the potatoes have been boiled to a fine starch paste, speedily ladle the whole malt mash, thin and thick, into the copper
Stir the mixture for an hour, keeping the temperature at from 144° to 156°F. all the time, so that the diastase of the malt may convert the starch into sugar and dextrine
When the white pasty liquid becomes transparent and thin, raise the fire to make the mash boil and keep it at its heat for ten minutes
Withdraw the fire and transfer the contents of the copper into the mash, work well, and let settle for half an hour
During this time, wash out the copper and quickly charge it once more with boiling water
Draw off the clear wort from the tun as usual and boil as soon as possible with the due proportion of hops
Add boiling water in any desired quantity to the drained mash for the second mashing

title: Puff Paste
description: Prepared with lemon-juice, butter, and flour.

ingredients.name: about a quarter of a pint of the coolest water
ingredients.sourceText: about a quarter of a pint of the coolest water

steps: Put the flour on the paste-board and make a hole in the centre
Put the yolk of an egg, lemon-juice, and salt in the hole
Mix the whole with cold water into a flexible paste with the right hand, handling it as little as possible
Squeeze all the buttermilk from the butter and wring it through a cloth
Roll out the paste and place the butter on this
Fold the edges of the paste over to hide the butter
Roll it out again to the thickness of a quarter of an inch
Fold over one-third, over which again pass the rolling-pin
Fold over the other third, thus forming a square
Place it with the ends, top, and bottom before you
Repeat the rolls and turns twice more
Flour a baking-sheet and put the paste on this
Let it remain in a cool place for half an hour
Roll twice more, turning it as before
Place it again in a cool place for a quarter of an hour
Give two more rolls, making seven in all

title: Sheep's Tongues in Tomato Sauce

steps: Wash the tongues in cold water, put them into a saucepan, cover them with cold water or stock, and bring to the boil, then skim well.
Either corned or fresh tongues will do for this dish. If corned, no salt is required; but if fresh ones are used, put in a dessertspoonful of salt.
Put in the vegetables and peppercorns and simmer gently for two hours.
Take them up, plunge them into cold water and remove the skin.
Trim them off and cut in half.
Make some tomato sauce by recipe given elsewhere. The liquor in which the tongues were boiled may be used for this if it is not too salt.
Lay the tongues in and simmer for another hour.
Dish carefully, boil up the sauce and pour over.
Garnish with chopped parsley.

Put a pint and a half of milk on to boil, and when it boils place on its surface as many table-spoonfuls of the whipped whites of eggs as will stand on it without touching each other
As each spoonful becomes cooked and assumes the appearance of snow, take it off and put on another, until all the whipped eggs are done
As you take off the snow from the milk, put it on a hair sieve to drain
Add to the milk a bit of lemon-peel, and sugar enough to sweeten it well
As soon as it has acquired the flavour of the lemon-peel, stir into it the yolks of eight eggs beaten up with a table-spoonful of orange-flower water
When of proper consistency, but not so thick as cream, pour it into a cream-dish
After it is cold, put the snow on the surface to make the sauce

title: To Boil Potatoes
description: Prepared with potatoes, salt, and water.
steps: Peel potatoes thinly, and well wash in cold water, but not soak; put them into a saucepan kept for this vegetable only.
Just cover them with cold water seasoned with salt, and bring to a boil.
Simmer very gently for about twenty minutes; test them with a fork, and if soft, strain off the water and toss them in a saucepan over the fire until they are dry.
If potatoes begin to break soon after they boil up, pour off nearly all the water, leaving only one inch at the bottom of the saucepan, and cook the potatoes slowly in this, then strain off and dry.
Potatoes that are very troublesome to boil often steam well; allow from an hour to one hour and a half, according to the quantity of water over which they are cooking.
